festivals.name: Maghe Sankranti
festivals.desc: First day of Magh — til laddoo, ghee & yam feasts; the big Khichdi fair at Gorkha's Malik Arjun temple.

festivals.name: Sonam Losar
festivals.desc: Tamang New Year — dances, momo feasts and family gatherings across the hills.

festivals.name: Maha Shivaratri
festivals.desc: Night of Lord Shiva — sadhus and devotees flock to Pashupatinath; bonfires of devotion.

festivals.name: Gyalpo Losar
festivals.desc: Himalayan Buddhist New Year — prayer flags, khapse cookies, family puja.

festivals.name: Fagu Purnima (Holi)
festivals.desc: Festival of colours — lola (bonfire) on the eve, then colours, water balloons and Laxmi Prasad Devkota's poem everywhere.

festivals.name: Ghode Jatra
festivals.desc: Horse parade at Tundikhel — Newari tradition chasing away the demon Tundi.

festivals.name: Bisket Jatra
festivals.desc: Bhaktapur's New Year chariot festival — giant lingo poles pulled through the streets.

festivals.name: Nepali New Year 2083
festivals.desc: Bikram Sambat New Year — a fresh start with parades, sweets and family time.

festivals.name: Buddha Jayanti
festivals.desc: Birth, enlightenment and mahaparinirvana of Buddha — lamps & prayers at Lumbini.

festivals.name: Janai Purnima & Raksha Bandhan
festivals.desc: Sacred thread (janai) changing for men, rakhi for siblings, and the khar-khadka at Gosaikunda.

festivals.name: Krishna Janmashtami
festivals.desc: Birth of Krishna — night vigils and the famous Krishna Mandir festival in Patan.

festivals.name: Gai Jatra
festivals.desc: Cow festival — processions, satire and comedy remembering the departed.

festivals.name: Indra Jatra
festivals.desc: Indra, god of rain — Kumari Jatra, the Living Goddess rides out, Bhairab masks and dancing.

festivals.name: Teej
festivals.desc: Women's festival — red dresses, fasting for husbands' long life, singing & dancing to Shiva.

festivals.name: Matatirtha Aunsi
festivals.desc: Mother's Day — remember and honour mothers; sweet feast of sagun.

festivals.name: Dashain
festivals.desc: The greatest festival — 15 days of victory of Durga over evil. Jamara, kites, swings (ping), tika & jamara on Dashami, and family reunions.

festivals.name: Tihar
festivals.desc: Festival of lights — crows, dogs and cows honoured, Laxmi puja with lights & rangoli, and Bhai Tika on the final day.

festivals.name: Chhath
festivals.desc: Worship of the Sun god — fasting women stand in rivers at dawn & dusk offering argha.
